title: Chapter 562
paragraphs: Chapter 562
Episode 147. The King of the Black Sea, Gliek (6)
Woooo…!
A cold and dark energy began to flow from Huroti. The energy of the stone of extinction wrapped around Ron like hundreds of black snakes.
That power became Ron's flesh, bones, and blood.
Hot breath spewed from her open mouth, and her broken body was being restored to its original form.
Ron's resurrection had a distinctly different form from those who had previously been revived by the power of the stone of extinction. It was incomparable to those mere spirits with physical forms.
It was the result of all the gods contained in the stone of extinction submitting to his will.
Since the disappearance of the god of hope, Numerus, the gods had never seen a human overcome death with nothing but their pure will, without his protection.
Nor had they ever heard of it.
It was such a shocking event that even the gods, who were trapped in the stone of extinction and dazed, could clearly recognize the miracle that Ron had caused, even while feeling fear from Gliek.
A brilliant miracle that could not be obscured by the bars of the stone of extinction, nor any other veil or deception, was illuminating this dark and frightening land.
'I thought such a near-perfect resurrection would be impossible without the completion of the stone of extinction...! Ron Hairan, how many more times do you intend to surprise me?'
Beyond admiration, awe.
Kelliark's heartbeat was speeding up. It was shameful to think that before Gliek awakened, he had looked down on Ron while bearing the power of the stone of extinction on his back.
Even Gliek seemed impressed.
The power of gods reviving the dead did not give him any excitement, but the miracle achieved by a single human alone was worth watching.
It wasn't leisure.
It was just that in such a lonely and long immortality, akin to punishment, he felt there wouldn't be another opportunity to see something so radiant.
Gliek also had expectations.
The human named Ron Hairan might become a being like themselves. Just as Kial and other Kings of the Black Sea had hoped for from Chiron.

Unfortunately, Dante's remaining will within Gliek was unable to recognize Ron's miracle. Since the beginning of the Black Sea transformation, Dante's will, which had been like a faint candle, was fading even faster.
Huuu…
Eventually, the black energy of the stone of extinction completely seeped in, and Ron took a deep breath and opened his eyes.
Her body was no longer weak, as it had been when she first awoke from her coma.

The newly reached realm of the void allowed her to vividly feel the strongest power she had ever experienced in her life, and the bones and organs she had lost as a price for unleashing the Tyrant Sword had all returned to their rightful place.
And thus, her body was fully restored.
The only thing that remained the same was one thing.
It was only the sorrow of having lost everything. The sorrow that moved him, even in death, could not be forgotten, and it was still tearing, scratching, and shattering his heart.
"Lord Ron."
Ron turned to Jin.
Jin could not dare to lift his head. He was suffocated by guilt for thinking of resurrecting him with the stone of extinction, and witnessing its execution firsthand.
Ron said nothing to Jin.
Instead, he gently patted Jin's shoulder. This was because he could not express his gratitude and consolation to Jin with any words he knew.
As Ron started walking slowly towards Gliek, he passed by Kelliark Zipfel without hesitation.
The stone of extinction no longer made a sound of trembling in fear.
It was not because he thought he could now defeat Gliek, but rather to set an example to the human named Ron Hairan.
Kelliark also followed him silently. Talaris, Stal, and the Black Knights naturally formed a line around Ron.

The magicians of the Zipfel, including the ghost army and Octavia, also entered the interior following the path that Kelliark had carved to get here, and almost simultaneously, the knights of Rosar and Runcandel joined the battlefield.
Unlike the troops of Zipfel, where it was hard to find a holy figure, Runcandel had almost no casualties.
Unlike Kelliark, who had rushed in to save Jin first, putting everything aside, Rosa had come alone to protect all the knights of her family.
'Did Kelliark resurrect Ron Hairan? No, that's not all.'
Rosa had not seen the miracle that Ron had caused firsthand.
But she knew. She knew that Ron was not just revived through the power of the stone of extinction.
This was because an indescribably pure and robust aura was emanating from his back. The meaning of that aura was clear.
'He keeps transcending his limits...'
Continuous transcendence.
The current Ron is stronger than the Ron of a while ago. Just his emanating energy alone made her body shudder.
However, Rosa also knew about the King of the Black Sea. She knew he was an entity that could not be defeated without Ascension.
In the past, she had seen Chiron, like Ron now, surpassing his limits every moment, just before reaching Ascension.
But even Chiron needed a considerable amount of time to climb the final step.
Rosa thought it was impossible for Ron to reach Ascension in this fight, no matter how much more he transcends.
Above all, she was worried that if she thought there was even a slight possibility, her judgement could unknowingly become clouded by that expectation.
All the knights of Runcandel, except for the Black Knights and the Black Sword Association 1st squad, took their positions towards the side where the Vamel Alliance was located.
They were ordered to quickly rescue Jin's companions and escape from Gliek once the battle began.
This was not a consideration for Jin.
If Rosa had purely considered Jin, she would never have given such an order.
The reason Rosa was saving Jin's companions was to prevent adding variables to an already tough fight.
If by any chance, his companions were to die, it would be unpredictable how Jin would react. At any other time, she might control him by force, but there would be no room for that against Gliek.
Like Talaris, Rosa also had the perception that there was only one thing they could do.
'If Chiron has already entered beyond the depths of the Black Sea... even with the use of Hidden Palace-Ju's frog's eye, a minimum of ten days will be needed.'
This meant they had to hold Gliek back for more than ten days.
This place was like the world's last line of defense.
The moment Gliek breaks through the knights and magicians gathered here and goes outside, the world will be under the threat of destruction from that day on.
Outside, there was no force capable of stopping the King of the Black Sea.
Kinzelo was still alive.
However, the fact that Kinzelo was not here, even though he was the only one who knew the identity of the white stone, meant that the situation they initially wanted was exactly this scene.
'Purely through battle, we can never hold out for that long.'
Rosa made eye contact with Talaris.
'So, the key must be Hidden Palace-Ju, not the much stronger Ron Hairan, nor the Zipfel who brought out the stone of extinction, nor us, Runcandel...'
The absolute seal of Hidden Palace.
That was the only thing that could buy time for Chiron to arrive. Rosa and Kelliark, the two who knew the sealing ability of Hidden Palace, were thinking the same.
The problem was whether the absolute seal of Hidden Palace could indeed buy more than ten days.
The shadow of Gliek loomed over those standing against him.
"State your name."
It was the first time Gliek had shown complete focus on someone other than Jin.
"Ron Hairan. The grandfather of the child you swallowed, the master of this land you are slaughtering, and the human who will kill you."
"Just now, your child's last will disappeared."
Ron was not swayed by his words. Now, emptiness could not have any influence on his inner self. Because he could no longer mourn.
The pain that had settled in his heart was like a sea. Anything added to the sea of sorrow would sink into the depths and disappear, and even Ron himself could not measure its size and depth.
"Is that so."
[Even death could not erase your pain. The only way to be saved from it is to become a being like me.]
Rashid turned to ash. The emblem of the Destroyer's Sword was being engraved on Ron's body once again.
He had no regrets about the life he had regained just a few minutes ago. Even if he were to destroy Gliek, what could life afterwards mean to him?
One of Gliek's hands, protruding from his massive body, descended in front of Ron. As if to grab him.
[So if you wish to escape from eternal pain, come to me.]
Instead of answering, Ron swung Rashid and severed that arm. However, the arm that fell to the ground was absorbed into the blackened ground and restored back to Gliek.
[You always fail to see what's right in front of you.]
The moment Gliek's attention towards Ron vanished, he once again focused his gaze on Jin, and the battle resumed straight away.
Hundreds of swords and spears pressed the humans faster and more precisely than before, and Ron lashed out at Rashid with a scream like a demon.
The ashen sword aura, spreading like wildfire, was clashing with the energy of chaos.
However, Gliek seemed to consider that even the Destroyer's Sword, unleashed in its perfect state by Ron, did not pose a significant threat.
Even if Rashid cut any part of his body, Gliek hardly blocked it and poured almost all his attacks on Jin.
Just as Rosa had predicted.
Gliek was even more wary of Talaris than Ron.
Because he saw through the fact that in the current world, there existed a being with the power to defy destiny, and that the humans planned to summon him here.
Just as Kial and Chiron had sensed the moment Gliek awoke, he too recognized their existence.
As the blackening took place and his consciousness awoke, their power felt more vivid.
Gliek thought that as long as he could prevent his half-god, who was fighting his brother, from coming here, there would be no problem.
However, even if the half-god did come here, the possibility of it being a threat was very low.

Because he couldn't be in good shape immediately after fighting Kial. In other words, whether Chiron came here or not, Gliek's restraining of Talaris was just an action to rule out even the smallest possibility.
Because the power to defy fate could always become dangerous, no matter when or under what circumstances.
"Hidden Palace-Ju. If you unleash the seal, how long can you hold up against that?"
Rosa stepped forward to Talaris and asked.
"...It will be difficult to surpass three days, Rosa Runcandel."
Upon hearing the answer, Rosa couldn't help but grit her teeth.
